concepts.title: The mapping class group $\mathrm{Mod}(S)$
concepts.blurb: $\mathrm{Mod}(S)$ is the group of orientation-preserving self-homeomorphisms (or diffeomorphisms) of an oriented surface $S$ modulo isotopy. For closed genus $g\ge 1$ it is finitely presented; the Birman exact sequence relates the mapping class groups of punctured and closed surfaces via point-pushing.

concepts.title: Dehn twists and generation
concepts.blurb: The Dehn twist $T_\gamma$ around a simple closed curve $\gamma$ generates a cyclic subgroup of $\mathrm{Mod}(S)$. The Lickorish–Humphries theorem says $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ is generated by twists about $2g+1$ explicit curves, with relations such as the lantern, chain, and hyperelliptic relations.

concepts.title: Nielsen–Thurston classification
concepts.blurb: Every mapping class is finite-order, reducible (preserves a multicurve), or pseudo-Anosov. A pseudo-Anosov $\varphi$ has a pair of transverse measured foliations and a dilatation $\lambda>1$ with $\varphi^*\mathcal{F}^u = \lambda\,\mathcal{F}^u$ and $\varphi^*\mathcal{F}^s = \lambda^{-1}\mathcal{F}^s$.

concepts.title: Teichmüller space and the $\mathrm{Mod}(S)$ action
concepts.blurb: Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(\Sigma_g)$ is the moduli of marked hyperbolic structures on $\Sigma_g$; for $g\ge 2$ it is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{6g-6}$. The mapping class group acts properly discontinuously on $\mathcal{T}$, and $\mathcal{M}_g = \mathcal{T}/\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ is the moduli space of Riemann surfaces — a complex orbifold of dimension $3g-3$.

concepts.title: 4-manifold fundamentals
concepts.blurb: In dimension 4 smooth and topological structures diverge sharply. Freedman: a closed simply-connected topological 4-manifold is determined by its intersection form on $H^2$ together with the Kirby–Siebenmann invariant. Donaldson: not every form is realised smoothly, and there are uncountably many smooth structures on $\mathbb{R}^4$.

concepts.title: Casson invariant and the Donaldson preview
concepts.blurb: For a homology 3-sphere $\Sigma$ the Casson invariant $\lambda(\Sigma)\in\mathbb{Z}$ is half the algebraic count of irreducible $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$. Casson's surgery formula computes $\lambda$ on Dehn surgeries; the Taubes–Floer reinterpretation as instanton homology is the bridge into Donaldson and Seiberg–Witten 4-manifold invariants.
